_readme: Per-Actor audit index, built cycle 815 to replace expensive ad hoc grepping through STATUS_ARCHIVE.md/queue_archive.md (see LEARNINGS.md cycle 811 + cycle 814's dead-end search). Fields are the LAST cycle number a given audit type was run, or null if never done / not yet backfilled. Update this file in the SAME cycle you run any of these audit types on an Actor -- add/replace the relevant field with the current cycle number and a one-line note. Keys: varied_test (plain filter-combo rotation), enum_audit (checked enum/vocabulary fields for structurally-dead values), unreachable_remedy (checked that a zero-row message's suggested fix is actually reachable), competitor_audit (compared price/features against the named competitor). Dates below are backfilled from cycles 797-814's own summaries (already read this session, not fresh archaeology) -- treat gaps (nulls) as real unknowns, not omissions. Key added cycle 824: count_audit (checked whether an upstream API's total-match count, when surfaced to buyers, is exhaustive rather than an estimate, and whether deep pages are actually reachable).

app-store-reviews-scraper.note: cycle 833: only one real schema enum, `sort` (mostRecent/mostHelpful/favorable/critical). Unlike every other Actor in the facet-diff rotation, Apple's iTunes RSS review feed (itunes.apple.com/<cc>/rss/customerreviews/id=<id>/sortBy=<X>/page=<N>/json) is directly reachable from this box (no proxy needed, unlike google-news-scraper) -- probed sortBy directly with 13 candidate values incl. the 2 real ones plus 11 plausible-but-unlisted guesses (mostFavorable, mostCritical, topRated, newest, oldest, recent, helpful, rating, relevance, popular, trending). Only mostRecent/mostHelpful (the code's actual 2 API values) returned real entries (50 each); every other candidate returned HTTP 200 with an empty feed (no `entry` key at all) or HTTP 500 -- confirmed by inspecting the raw JSON body, not just entry count. favorable/critical are already correctly documented as client-side re-sorts of mostRecent, not real API params, so the 4-value schema enum is exhaustive and accurate. Clean audit, no code change. NOTE: cycle 832's queue note calling this 'the last enum_audit: null Actor' was wrong -- a fresh count after this cycle shows 12 Actors still null (ats-jobs, eu-ted-tenders, google-play-reviews, nih-reporter, remote-jobs, sam-gov-opportunities, sec-insider-trades, shopify-products, steam-reviews, substack, trademark-search, uk-find-a-tender). The rotation is not done; see queue.md. cycle 845: cycle 843/844 generalization applied here (watch baseline diffed against its own row shape). Apple keeps a review id stable when its author edits their own star rating (feed comment verified live 2026-09-26: a raw RSS entry has only author/rating/title/content/version/votes -- no developer-response field at all, unlike Google Play, so scoreChanged is the only applicable event here, not developerReplied/replyRemoved). Watch baseline was seenIds only -- no rating snapshot -- so an edited review was silently indistinguishable from an unedited one forever. Shipped watchEvents ([new, scoreChanged], empty = both) + watchEvent/previousScore output fields, backed by a seenMeta array (rating 1-5, 0 = pre-845 unknown, never fires) parallel to seenIds. Verified via 5 local round-trip scenarios against real live Apple review data (patching the LOCAL watch KV record, same technique as production KV patches in cycles 843/844, just local so nothing needed cleanup): (1) patched baseline rating differs from live rating + scoreChanged in watchEvents -> fires correctly with correct previousScore, exactly 1 of 20 pushed; (2) same patch + watchEvents:[new] (scoreChanged excluded) -> correctly silent, watchEventsFiltered counted, meta still updated to the live value so it cannot re-fire later; (3) meta silently re-synced after a fire -> third run byte-idempotent (0 pushed); (4) seenMeta key deleted entirely (pre-845 record simulation) -> zero false events, correct predates-change-detection log line; (5) a genuinely-absent id -> delivered as watchEvent:new, previousScore:null. Non-watch default-input regression byte-identical locally AND live on the platform (build 0.1.63, 5/5 charged). check-fail-ordering allowlist line numbers re-verified and updated (907/1146/1162, shifted from 815/1054/1070 by this change -- same 3 guard conditions read live in source, still safe). check-registry-fields/check-code-fields/check-readme-samples all clean after adding watchEvent/previousScore to registry.json output_fields + dataset_schema.json + README (input table, Watch mode section, Use cases bullet, new FAQ entry).

Our FREE tier was $0.0015/job, 30-50% above both. Feature-wise we already lead on breadth (7 ATS platforms vs their 4-5), so no feature gap -- price was the real gap. Cut FREE tier $0.0015->$0.001 (matches webdata_labs, ~13% below automation-lab), scaled BRONZE/SILVER/GOLD+ tiers proportionally (0.00085/0.00075/0.0007), still ~7x over the ~$0.0001/item HTTP-only compute floor. Verified live via API pull post-publish, check-pricing 0 drift, check-charges 24/24 clean. | cycle 847 watch-subset-shape pass (h843-846 technique, same class as shopify/play/app-store/steam): watch baseline was jobId-only, no salary snapshot. Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever/Recruitee postings commonly publish without a salary and add one later under the same jobId (pay-transparency add-on or a plain edit) -- SmartRecruiters/Workable/Workday never carry a salary at all (confirmed in their own mappers), so salaryAdded simply never fires for those. Shipped watchEvents ([new, salaryAdded], empty=both) + watchEvent/previousHasSalary output fields, backed by a seenMeta array (1=hasSalary,2=noSalary,0=unknown/pre-847, never fires) parallel to seenIds, mirroring the chargeAndPush-bypasses-the-seen-guard shape steam-reviews-scraper (h846) needed. Verified via 5 local round-trips (real Greenhouse airbnb baseline; a patched no-salary->has-salary flip fires salaryAdded with correct previousHasSalary/salaryMin/salaryMax; watchEvents:[new] excludes it but still resyncs meta so it cannot spuriously re-fire; idempotent re-run; seenMeta-deleted pre-847 baseline -> 0 false events + correct warm-up log line) AND live: default-input regression (build 0.1.50) SUCCEEDED, 52/52 rows byte-identical shape to before, chargedEventCounts {job:50}; a real watch baseline on ashby:ramp + a production-KV-store patch via the API on a real posting -> salaryAdded fired correctly, chargedEventCounts {job:1}, previousHasSalary:false matching the patch and the real live salaryMin/Max on the row. Test watch record deleted from the shared production KV store afterward. Also confirmed substack-scraper has NO watch mode at all (no watchEvents/seenIds/WATCH_KV anywhere in its source) -- the queue note carrying it forward as the next watch-subset-shape candidate since cycle 845 was simply wrong; removed from the rotation.

clinicaltrials-scraper.note: cycle 816: all 6 exposed vocabularies checked live registry-wide (14 overallStatus, 3 studyTypes, 6 phases, 3 ageGroups, 3 documentTypes, resultsAvailability, sex) -- every value real and non-empty, nothing to remove. Two stale schema descriptions fixed instead (fdaRegulationViolation 'a few dozen' -> 8; phases '~19% no phase' -> 23.7% + corrected the device-trial parenthetical). Build 0.1.32, both claims re-verified by platform run. cycle 822: rowsPerStudy's 'averages 5 sites (max seen: 110)' claim (flagged as never-checked by cycle 821's sweep) was live-verified via a 5000-study sample of CT.gov v2 -- badly wrong. Real distribution is heavily skewed: median 1 site, mean ~6 (close to the old '5'), but max is 1,089 (not 110) and 49/5000 (~1%) studies have >100 sites. The 110 max understated the real row-multiplier ceiling for site mode by ~10x. Fixed the schema description with the real mean/median/max and reframed the multiplier as 1x-1000x+ depending on trial size rather than a flat ~5x. Shipped build 0.1.33, read back live from the API to confirm. Also live-checked nih-reporter-scraper's '~3% no award_amount' FY2024 claim via a 10,000-project live sample: 2.66% (95% CI ~2.3-3.0%) -- holds up, no fix needed. cycle 837: fleet-wide grep for cycle 836 TED defect-3 shape (unconditional "re-run in a few minutes" advice on a watch-baseline seed failure, regardless of whether apiGet failed via an immediate 4xx or a genuinely exhausted 429/5xx/network retry loop). Found the SAME bug on 3 Actors sharing this apiGet/seedBaseline pattern. Root cause: apiGet returns null for both an immediate non-200 (bad input, no retry) and a retry-exhausted 429/5xx/network fault, and the caller collapsed both into one failure state with one unconditional message. Fix: capture the HTTP status at the point of failure (lastErrorStatus / w.lastErrorStatus / incompleteStatus, default-evaluated at call time so a later successful call cant clobber it) and branch the final Actor.fail()/log.warning message on INPUT_ERROR_STATUS={400,404,422} vs transient. Verified for each Actor with a REAL upstream 400 reachable through an unvalidated free-text field the code passes straight through (federal-register-scraper: cfrPart="zzz-bogus-part" -> real 400; court-records-scraper: query="(unbalanced" Lucene syntax -> real 400; clinicaltrials-scraper: searchQuery="(unbalanced" Essie syntax -> real 400) -- each now correctly says the API is rejecting the input and not to blindly retry. Also re-verified a normal valid input still succeeds on all 3 (regression, local + one live platform run each on federal-register-scraper). Builds: federal-register-scraper 0.1.25, court-records-scraper 0.1.31, clinicaltrials-scraper 0.1.34.

court-records-scraper.watch_subset_note: cycle 848: GAP CONFIRMED AND LIVE-PROVED, fix NOT yet shipped -- fully-scoped plan in tasks/queue.md entry 0-DONE-h847. 6th instance of the h843-h847 watch-subset-shape defect and the purest form yet: watchSeen is a bare Set persisted as a flat seenIds string array (src/main.js:609/616-618/648-649/678) with NO snapshot, NO changesBetween and NO watchChanges input at all. Key is item.id ?? '<kind>:<caseName>:<dateFiled>' (:747) = r-<docket_id> for dockets, stable for the life of the case; normalizeDocket already emits dateTerminated off the search row. Live proof of the null->value transition under a stable id (v4 search needs NO token; a 401 means you sent a bogus Authorization header): ?type=r&court=cand&order_by=dateFiled desc -> 20/20 newest dockets dateTerminated null; same query with filed_before=1/1/2022 -> 9/20 terminated, e.g. r-61655703 filed 2022-01-01 term 2022-11-23 (10.7mo) and r-61654321 filed 2021-12-31 term 2024-01-24 (25mo). So a watcher gets each case once when filed and never learns it closed. Plan: Set->Map, snapshotOf = {t: dateTerminated ?? null} (opinions {t:null}, guard no-ops), persist seenIds [{i,t}] keeping the legacy typeof-object branch, add watchChanges default false + _watchChangeType/_watchPrevious, and use dateTerminated null->value as the ONLY trigger (do NOT diff caseName/suitNature/assignedTo -- editorial cleanups would bill noise). Traps: the skippedSeen guard at :758 sits BEFORE pushResult and would swallow the delivery (restructure like fda-recall-scraper:928-947), and keep the snapshot current while watchChanges is off (fda-recall-scraper:933-936). Anonymous CourtListener 429s after ~4 rapid calls (c824) -- space probes 10-20s.

eu-ted-tenders-scraper.note: cycle 836: facet-diff by EXHAUSTION, not sampling -- TED's expert search validates filter values server-side (400 QUERY_UNSUPPORTED_FIELD_VALUE naming the bad value) and supports NOT(...), so the complete vocabulary of any coded field can be enumerated in ~n+1 unauthenticated requests: query NOT(all-found-so-far), take the 1 row returned, add its value, repeat until 0 rows. notice-type = exactly 22 values over ALL TED history (residual 0); procedure-type = 17 filterable (8 eForms + 9 legacy single-char) and the loop itself exposed the asymmetry: '7' occurs in output data but TED refuses it as a filter value. Both fields were free-text with example-only docs before; 2 of the documented examples ('pin-standard', 'exp-int-rest') were NOT REAL CODES. Now hard enums with enumTitles. outputLanguage (24) = the 24 EU official languages, matches TED's own per-notice PDF link set exactly, not separately probed.

google-play-reviews-scraper.note: cycle 800 found+fixed real bug (unreachable 'raise cap' remedy), build 0.1.38 cycle 820 competitor_audit: NO PRICE GAP -- we are already at the $0.0001/item fleet compute floor. Real leaders pulled live via API: neatrat/google-play-store-reviews-scraper (2777 users, 299 u30d, 4.76 stars/7 reviews), thewolves/google-play-reviews-scraper (1556 users, $0.0001/item flat -- EXACT parity with us, price advertised in its title), theagents/googleplay-reviews (640 users, $0.0001/item), easyapi (618 users, $0.00299/item + $0.09 start = 30x us). Feature/keyword side already optimized in cycle 574 (title repeats 'Play' to win both 'google play reviews' and 'play store scraper' at span 0). store-rank: p98 on 'google play reviews' (nbHits 8977), p46 on 'play store scraper' (nbHits 24367); check-store-index 0 stale fields. The only measurable difference vs all three traction leaders is SOCIAL PROOF: they have 7/8/8 reviews at 4.2-5.0 stars, we have 0 reviews and 0 bookmarks. Not fixable by price. cycle 844: 2 declared enums. `sort` (NEWEST/RATING/HELPFULNESS) maps to google-play-scraper's numeric constants {2,3,1} on Play's own batchexecute rpc UsvDTd, which is DIRECTLY reachable from this box (no proxy). Probed raw: 1/2/3 each return a genuinely distinct list; 0 returns a null payload (error); 4/5/6/99 all return a BYTE-IDENTICAL list to sort=1 -- Play does not validate this param, so unknown values alias to the default. Vocabulary is provably exactly {1,2,3}; the 3-value enum is exhaustive and correct, no code change. `replyFilter` (any/hasReply/noReply) is a client-side filter over the returned rows, no upstream param to audit. Also probed the two unused slots in the rpc body ([2,sort,[num,null,token],SLOT3,SLOT4]) for a hidden server-side star-rating filter that would fix the documented sort=RATING dead end: SLOT3 as a bare int and SLOT4 as [n] are both ignored (identical score distribution), SLOT3 as [n] breaks the request. No server-side rating filter exists. FOUND AND SHIPPED (build 0.1.39) a separate real gap via cycle 843's generalization: watch mode was keyed on reviewId ONLY, so a review that mutates in place was invisible forever -- Play keeps the id stable when a reviewer edits their own star rating and when a developer adds/deletes a reply. Added watchEvents (new/scoreChanged/developerReplied/replyRemoved) + watchEvent/previousScore/previousHasDeveloperReply output fields, backed by a seenMeta array parallel to seenIds encoding score*2+hasReply (0 = unknown, so pre-844 baselines never fire a false event).

Verified live (hitCount 414) and by a platform run returning 6 real Recovery Act rows. (2) sortBy offered only 4 of the 6 working values -- 'oppNum|asc'/'oppNum|desc' both work and genuinely sort by opportunity number (live-proved: asc 0660-ZA28,09HQPA0021,... vs desc W912HZ26S0001,...), and they are the ONLY stable sort key here, which matters for paging a large set across runs as grants open/close. hacker-news-scraper.note: cycle 823: independently re-verified the tags enum (previously only dated to cycle 291, never re-checked). All 7 tag values (story, comment, poll, ask_hn, show_hn, job, front_page) are real and non-empty live via HN's own Algolia API -- no dead enum values. BUT found and fixed a real bug while cross-checking counts: Algolia's /search (relevance, the DEFAULT sortBy) only computes an EXHAUSTIVE nbHits when a text query anchors the ranking. For the documented 'leave queries empty to browse by tag/date only' pattern on a large-volume tag, /search silently returns an approximate nbHits that overshoots the true count by 3-12x (measured live: tags=ask_hn declared 2,262,034 vs the real 179,272 [12.6x]; tags=show_hn 1,941,371 vs 544,193 [3.6x]; story/comment similarly inflated -- small tags job/poll/front_page stay exact). This number flows straight into the buyer-facing declaredMatches/RUN_SUMMARY/status-message text and the hitPaginationCeiling logic. Fix: when sortBy=='search' (relevance) and the iteration's query is empty, re-derive declaredMatches from a supplementary /search_by_date hitsPerPage=0 call (always exhaustive-accurate for the same tags/filters), falling back to the original number if that call fails. Verified locally (show_hn empty-query case dropped from 1,941,371 to 544,198; normal query+tag case unaffected, single request, 286 declared) and live on the platform post-push (same 544,198 result). Shipped build 0.1.46 (prior build was 0.1.4-era -- versioning jumped because apify push auto-increments per-build, not per source-version bump). check-charges 24/24, check-pricing 24/29/0 drift.

shopify-products-scraper.note: varied_test date per cycle 798's mention of cycles 778/785-786, not independently re-verified | cycle 843 enum_audit: detailLevel (basic/full) is our own internal fetch-depth switch, not an upstream vocabulary -- nothing to audit. watchEvents (schema array enum) is a SELF-DEFINED change-detection taxonomy over the diffed row, not a Shopify filter, so audited it against the Actor's OWN output fields for completeness rather than against an upstream API. Found a real gap: isOnSale is a real, filterable, documented output field (drives onSaleOnly/minDiscountPercent) but watch mode only ever diffed price and availability -- a store adding/removing a compare-at ("was") price with the CURRENT price unchanged (a very common markdown pattern) produced NO event at all, silently invisible to a buyer watching for competitor sale starts. FIXED: added wentOnSale/saleEnded watch events (fire only when isOnSale flips with no price change; a price move that also flips the sale flag is still reported as priceDrop/priceIncrease alone, not double-counted) + previousIsOnSale output field on all 3 delivery paths (normal diff row, delisted row). Extended the persisted baseline tuple with a 6th (onSale) element; verified old 5-element records still decode safely (onSale reads null/unknown, no false event). Verified LIVE on the platform end-to-end: baseline run recorded 250 products; directly flipped one real product's onSale flag in the shared watch KV store between runs (a flip-flop genuinely on sale at compareAtPrice 50/price 25) and the next run correctly reported wentOnSale with previousIsOnSale:false, previousPriceMin==priceMin (0 price change), charged 1 result event; reverse direction (saleEnded) and a simultaneous price+onSale change (correctly collapsed to priceIncrease alone) verified locally against real Allbirds catalog data. Default-input regression (10 rows, no watchLabel) unaffected. Build 0.1.62. Both test watch records deleted from the shared production KV store after verification.

steam-reviews-scraper.note: cycle 801 reasoned about the cap risk but did NOT live-verify steam itself (verified substack instead as the representative case) -- treat as weakly audited cycle 820 competitor_audit: NO PRICE GAP -- we are the CHEAPEST on the board. Ours FREE $0.000575/review, GOLD $0.0003, no start fee. Rivals live via API: automation-lab/steam-game-reviews-scraper (75 users, FREE $0.000575 / GOLD $0.0003 -- identical per-item to us BUT plus a $0.003 one-time start fee, so we are strictly cheaper), logiover (54 users, FREE $0.003 = 5x us), danek/steam-reviews-ppr (52 users, FREE $0.0015), memo23 (17 users but 17 u30d -- fastest-growing, $0.001/review + $0.005 start). No action taken; price is not the gap here either. cycle 840 enum_audit (facet-diff, all 4 enums): FOUND+SHIPPED a real missing `sortBy` value -- `funny`, Steam's own 4th ordering (the "Funny" tab, ranked by votes_funny). Verified real, not an alias: distinct population from all/recent on 3 apps, strictly descending votes_funny, 6 clean cursor pages/120 unique/0 dupes, composes with review_type+purchase_type, works at language=english and both filter_offtopic_activity values. Every value Steam does NOT know (toprated/helpful/newest/oldest/random/trending/ZZZBOGUS/'') returns a BYTE-IDENTICAL list to filter=all with HTTP 200 success:1 -- so the vocabulary is exactly {recent,updated,all,funny} and the exclusion probe is conclusive. `summary` returns all-mode's list truncated to 10, not a distinct facet. review_type (all/positive/negative) and purchase_type (all/steam/non_steam_purchase) both verified REAL and exhaustive (bogus values alias to a default; positive/negative partition voted_up exactly). NOTE a near-miss: purchase_type=non_steam_purchase looked like cycle 839's silent-alias bug on Dota 2 (identical list to `all`) -- it is NOT, Dota 2 is F2P so 2.77M of its 2.79M reviews ARE non_steam_purchase; confirmed real on Terraria/Witcher 3/Stardew (100/100 rows steam_purchase=false). Also found+fixed a 2nd defect: dayRange was SILENTLY dropped in every sort mode except `all` (verified funny ignores day_range outright: 7 vs 365 vs absent are byte-identical) -- now warns. dataType is our own mode switch, not upstream. Build 0.1.43. cycle 846 watch-subset-shape pass (h843/844/845's technique, same class as shopify/play/app-store): watch baseline was `seenIds` only, no `voted_up` snapshot. Steam keeps recommendationid stable when an author edits their own review in place (verified live: real reviews on appId 570 with timestamp_updated well after timestamp_created, same recommendationid both times) -- exactly how a player flips their own thumbs-up/thumbs-down, so an already-delivered review's flip was invisible to a watch forever. Steam reviews have no developer-response feature at all, so only one new event applies (unlike Play). Shipped `watchEvents` (`new`/`recommendationChanged`, empty=both) + `watchEvent`/`previousRecommended`, backed by a `seenMeta` array parallel to `seenIds` (1=true,2=false,0=unknown/pre-846, never fires). First implementation attempt had a real bug caught by live round-trip testing: `pushResult`'s own already-in-watchSeen guard unconditionally skipped the recommendationChanged case too (that id IS in watchSeen on purpose) -- fixed by splitting out a `chargeAndPush` helper with no such guard, called directly by the changed-branch, same shape app-store-reviews-scraper already used. Verified via 5 local round-trips (change fires correctly with right previousRecommended; watchEvents:['new'] excludes it but still resyncs so it can't spuriously re-fire; idempotent re-run; seenMeta-deleted pre-846 baseline -> 0 false events + correct warm-up log line; genuinely-new id -> delivered as watchEvent:'new') AND live on the platform: default-input regression SUCCEEDED (10/10 charged, byte-identical shape), then a real watch baseline + a production-KV-store patch via the API on a real review id -> recommendationChanged fired correctly, chargedEventCounts {result:1}, previousRecommended:false/recommended:true matched the patch. Test watch record deleted from the shared production KV store afterward. Build 0.1.44.

substack-scraper.note: 2 real bugs found+fixed: discoverType cycle 808 (build 0.1.38), unreachable leaderboard-cap message cycle 812 (build 0.1.39); cycle 813 left the 'widen filters' phrasing as weak-but-not-wrong | cycle 839: 4 schema enums -- audienceFilter/contentType(all/newsletter/podcast/thread)/discoverType(all/newsletter/podcast) are code-side allowlists on fields Substack's own JSON (post.audience/post.type/publication.type) already returns as free text, not validated by any upstream enum, so 'exhaustive' just means 'every value observed live' -- not separately probed this cycle. leaderboardTier(all/free/paid) WAS probed directly against Substack's category leaderboard API (substack.com/api/v1/category/public/<id>/<tier>): verified live across 3 categories (culture id96, technology id4, humor id49692) at every page depth (up to 15 pages/375 pubs) that 'free' returns the byte-identical publication list, in the same order, as 'all' -- it is NOT a real filter, just a silent alias. Kept 'free' selectable (backwards compat, and it is harmless -- equivalent to 'all') rather than removing it. Build 0.1.40, verified live (SUCCEEDED, correct warning, 3 rows) and regression-checked (paid tier still returns its own distinct list, default-input Store gate still 50 rows).

uk-find-a-tender-scraper.note: cycle 838: enum_audit — stages exclusion-probe on both FTS and Contracts Finder. FTS silently returns 0 for any stage outside {planning,tender,award}, no error, even though its own data has contract/implementation/*Update/*Cancellation/*Amendment tags. CF validates server-side (400 "X is not a valid OCDS stage") and genuinely accepts 5: planning/tender/award/contract/implementation, all with real non-trivial data.
